intro: Like much of the river-facing part of Brooke County, land around Hooverson Heights sat between industrial development on one side and quiet farmland on the other, and the mineral rights under it reflect whichever side of that line a given tract fell on. Confirming which pattern applies to your family's interest starts with the recorded deed.

sections.heading: Industrial edge versus farmland interior
paragraphs: Tracts closer to the river and the mills sometimes had minerals conveyed along with an industrial sale, while tracts further back kept mineral rights with the farming family through generations. We confirm which applies to your specific tract.

sections.heading: Deep leasing reaching this stretch of Brooke County
paragraphs: Operators targeting Utica and Point Pleasant rock have leased acreage throughout Brooke County, and a Hooverson Heights tract may carry a modern deep-rights lease layered over an older shallow-well lease.

sections.heading: Confirming heirs before pricing an interest
paragraphs: Mineral interests here have typically split among descendants over multiple generations without formal partition. We trace the deed and probate record to confirm your exact percentage before naming a figure.
In practice that often means finding a will that names some but not all of the current owners, with the remaining share passing by intestate succession to whoever else was entitled to inherit.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically hold a Hooverson Heights-area interest?

faqs.question: What if my share of the tract was never given its own deed?
